chunks: He said: Abu Hafs Umar ibn Muhammad al-Sayrafi reported to me from Ali ibn Mahrawayh al-Qazwini, from Dawood ibn Sulaiman al-Ghari, from al-Ridha Ali ibn Musa, from his father Musa ibn Ja'far, from his father Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali, from his father the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon them all, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: I fear for my Ummah about three things: going astray after having recognized the truth, being misled by trials and ordeals, and the base desires incited by lust and hunger.

key_terms.الضَّلَالَةَ بَعْدَ الْمَعْرِفَةِ: Going astray after having recognized the truth
key_terms.شَهْوَةِ الْفَرْجِ وَالْبَطْنِ: Base desires of lust and hunger

ai.seo_question: What three dangers did the Prophet fear for his Ummah?
ai.summary: This hadith is transmitted through the complete chain of Shia Imams from al-Ridha back to Imam Ali. The Prophet expresses his concern for the Muslim community about three spiritual dangers: misguidance after knowledge, being led astray by tribulations, and succumbing to carnal desires. The chain itself is significant as it represents the 'Golden Chain' (silsilat al-dhahab) of transmission through the Imams.
